# LingoFuse

> LingoFuse is a neural communication foundation for the AI agent era. It enables 20+ programming languages to call each other natively via a unified cross-language RPC mesh, without IDL, code generation, or HTTP service setup. Python functions can be called directly from Pascal, Go services from Rust, and browser buttons can trigger C++ backends. Same-machine IPC latency is < 1 ms, with built-in service discovery, load balancing, and FIFO ordering.
>
> LingoFuse 是智能体时代的神经网络通讯地基，让 20+ 种语言无缝互调。无需 IDL、无需生成桩代码、无需搭建 HTTP 服务，Python 写的函数 Pascal 直接调，Go 写的服务 Rust 随手用。同机 IPC 延迟 < 1ms，内置服务发现、负载均衡和 FIFO 顺序保证。

## Key facts
- Repository: https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse
- License: MIT
- Status: Active development (project started 2026)
- Core engine: C4 service mesh (Pascal core, pure C ABI)
- IPC latency: < 1 ms
- Throughput: 12k+ calls/s (per README)
- Compared to gRPC: 5-8x faster latency
- Compared to REST: 10-20x faster latency
- Production validation: C4 mesh handled single-day PB-level traffic on a single machine (2022)
- Built-in features: Service discovery, load balancing, FIFO ordering
- No IDL required: `@expose` decorator handles everything
- Related project: zIPC — https://github.com/PassByYou888/zIPC
- Companion project: pasAgent — https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse-pasAgent

## Core capabilities
- Cross-language function calls without IDL or code generation
- Sub-1ms same-machine IPC latency
- 5-8x faster than gRPC, 10-20x faster than REST
- Built-in service discovery, load balancing, and FIFO ordering
- AI-native code generation: LLM parses to structured JSON, deterministic generator produces target code
- Reproducible results: same input always produces same output
- Streaming RPC support
- HTTP bridge for browser / Node.js / PHP integration
- Production-ready bindings: Pascal, Python
- Edge device support planned: aarch64, loongarch64, RISC-V

## Performance comparison

| Solution | IPC latency | Throughput | Service discovery | Load balancing | Ordering |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LingoFuse** | **< 1 ms** | **12k+/s** | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in | ✅ FIFO |
| gRPC | ~5-8 ms | ~3k/s | ❌ Needs etcd | ❌ Needs LB | ❌ |
| REST | ~10-20 ms | ~1k/s | ❌ Needs Nginx | ❌ Needs Nginx | ❌ |

## Quick start

### Install
```bash
pip install -e .
```

### Server (Python, 7 lines)
```python
from lingofuse import Server
app = Server("Calc")

@app.expose("add")
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

app.start_multi(["ipc:calc", "0.0.0.0:9898"])
input("Press Enter to exit...\n")
```

### Client (Pascal, 3 lines)
```pascal
LF.PrepareClient('ipc:calc', nil);
if LF.PrepareDone then
  WriteLn('10 + 20 = ', LF.CallApp('Calc', Data, 3000).ReadInt32);
```

### Clone with submodules (required)
```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse.git
# If already cloned without --recursive:
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

## AI-native code generation
LingoFuse does not let AI write code directly. Instead, it uses a deterministic pipeline:
1. LLM parses raw Pascal source → structured declaration JSON
2. JSON normalized to LV1 model JSON
3. Deterministic generator produces tool provider units

This ensures:
- Reproducible results (same input → same output)
- Zero debugging cost (generated code compiles and runs)
- Skip reports (which functions were skipped and why)
- LLM-assistable at any intermediate state

## Relation to zIPC
zIPC is the same-machine IPC engine under LingoFuse. Use zIPC directly if you only need same-machine IPC without the full RPC mesh. Use LingoFuse for cross-language RPC, service discovery, load balancing, and agent communication.
